title: dedicated-autoscaler: throughput guarantees, burst controls and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: Production fleets running in Dedicated have seen tail latency and burst-induced queueing when transient traffic spikes exceed slot throughput. Operators need: (1) a configurable per-fleet throughput guarantee to provide predictable baseline capacity, (2) burst controls that let customers specify temporary capacity headroom and decay, and (3) better utilization and burst reporting in the Console so SREs can reason about cost vs. performance.

This PR implements a coordinated change across the autoscaler, token-bucket admission controller, telemetry pipeline, and Console reporting: - Add per-fleet throughput_guarantee config (tokens/sec) that the autoscaler will maintain as a soft target. - Introduce burst_window and burst_decay config fields and a token-bucket allocator that enforces burst headroom while preventing long-lived oversubscription. - Augment utilization metrics (fleet_util_pct, burst_consumed_tokens, burst_headroom_remaining) emitted from the autoscaler. - Add deduped reporting and new Grafana panels for burst vs baseline utilization. - Expose a Console API and UI flags for configuring throughput guarantees and burst controls with a rollout guard.

Implementation notes: - Autoscaler: refactor scaling loop to consider guaranteed throughput as a baseline when computing desired slots; added a burst_token_bucket submodule with O(1) allocation semantics. - Token-bucket admission: admission now consults fleet-level bucket, per-priority short-circuit logic added for high-priority customers. - Telemetry: migrate three new metrics through the OTLP pipeline; added tags for fleet_id, priority, and rollout_tag. - Console: new route /fleets/:id/throughput-controls and a small React form with validation and an audit log entry on changes.

Testing & validation: - Unit tests for token-bucket edge cases and autoscaler decision logic. - Integration tests in perf-canary to replay spike traces and validate no regression in 99th percentile latency. - Manual QA: validated Console form flows and audit logs in staging.

Rollout & safety: - Feature gated behind rollout tag and defaulted off for all fleets. - Canary rollout to internal customers and one pilot enterprise customer. - Fallback: autoscaler respects existing per-fleet slot limits; burst settings default to conservative values.

Related: Linear ENG-5234, ENG-5389. SUP ticket SUP-4121 reported repeated burst queueing incidents; this PR addresses the root cause and provides observability required for follow-ups.

release_notes:
- Added per-fleet throughput guarantees to stabilize baseline capacity and reduce tail latency during spikes.
- Introduced configurable burst controls (burst_window, burst_decay) to allow controlled temporary headroom.
- Emitted new utilization metrics (fleet_util_pct, burst_consumed_tokens, burst_headroom_remaining) and Console panels for visibility.
- Feature is rollout-gated and default-off; admins can enable per-fleet from Console.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: enable for internal fleets first, monitor fleet_util_pct and burst_headroom_remaining. If autoscaler.throughput_clamped_count spikes, reduce throughput_guarantee or increase reserved capacity. See docs/ops/dedicated_throughput_guarantees.md for rollback steps.
changelog_summary: Enhancement: Dedicated autoscaler now supports throughput guarantees and burst controls with improved utilization reporting
